outcome: Cervical condition (Bishop score and ultrasound cervical length)
cohort: 245 women who underwent labour induction during their 41st week of gestation
finding: A very unfavourable Bishop score upon admission (Bishop score <2) and no history of previous deliveries significantly increased the cost of labour induction and predicted the likelihood of a caesarean section.
mod_finding: The abstract does not report on differences in perinatal outcomes or costs by mode of delivery, but it does mention that the likelihood of successful trial of labor is a key factor influencing the cost of labor induction.
